Yes. cfo.ai is required, and it is not part of the agent code. It is a separate business plan for Friction Fixer: pricing, costs, revenue, and runway. Judges score the use of neatlogs, Entire, and cfo.ai together at 25%, and the demo has to show all three.

The Discord message matches the [hackathon page](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon). Submissions open Monday, October 12, at 7:00 PM IST, with a planned close around 11:55 PM IST. The exact submit steps are not live yet. What you need ready before then is the story, the demo, and the evidence in the repo. The quote post will ask for your team, project name, public repo, and demo link. The cfo.ai plan goes in the repo and in the video, not as its own form.

**Do this on cfo.ai**

1. Sign up at [cfo.ai](https://cfo.ai). A card is required. Right after signup, cancel the subscription in Settings, then Billing, so you are not billed. The neatHack team sends the cfo.ai credits directly.
2. On the starting card, pick a different business and estimate the numbers. Friction Fixer has no accounting history, so do not connect a bank or books.
3. Paste this to Ari:

> Build a 12-month plan for Friction Fixer, a SaaS where agents read a site's analytics, open one GitHub pull request per run, and keep or undo the change. Label every number as an assumption. Price it as a monthly subscription per connected site. Costs are model calls per run (analyst, builder, reviewer), hosting, and a small fixed monthly cost. Show monthly revenue, cost, gross margin, and cash runway for a base case and a growth case. Say what price covers the cost of one run.

4. Open the pages it builds and check that pricing, cost per run, revenue, and runway are all on them. If a number is wrong, tell Ari to change that assumption.
5. On the page, use Share, then Create link. No password. Put that link in the README where it says `cfo.ai business plan`.

**In the demo, about 20 seconds**

cfo.ai sits outside the agent loop. You asked Ari to model Friction Fixer, it built the plan from stated assumptions, and the result is the price, the cost of a run, and how long the cash lasts. Show the shared page, not just the chat.
